lines: {target}? Green stalks can hide quick trouble. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Bamboo Jungle, tell them: Keep a path cut behind you. I will be at the lectern.
Bamboo crowds the eye and the feet. I will write that warning down.
Bamboo Jungle is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Bamboo Jungle as a green wall that rustles like whispers. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Leaves crowd close enough to hide anything. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Jungle, tell them: Cut a path and remember which vines you passed. I will be at the lectern.
The green is loud even when nothing moves. I will write that warning down.
Jungle is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Jungle as a hot forest that keeps secrets well. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Mud holds boots longer than plans. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Mangrove Swamp, tell them: Step on roots and keep slime in mind. I will be at the lectern.
Thick roots make every hurry foolish. I will write that warning down.
Mangrove Swamp is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Mangrove Swamp as muddy water with a grip on your ankles. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Thin jungle still keeps thick surprises. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Sparse Jungle, tell them: Do not trust open patches too quickly. I will be at the lectern.
Vines and shadows take turns hiding things. I will write that warning down.
Sparse Jungle is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Sparse Jungle as green country pretending to be easier than it is. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Mud and water both remember footsteps. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Swamp, tell them: Watch slimes, witches, and the slow ground. I will be at the lectern.
Fog makes close things feel far. I will write that warning down.
Swamp is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Swamp as wet land that grabs at ankles and plans. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
